To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients on cyclosporine have higher numbers of circulating endothelium than patients not on calcineurin-inhibitors and patients not on cyclosporin.

renal transplant recipients on a cyclosporine-based regimen had elevated numbers of endothelial cells in the peripheral blood in comparison with healthy subjects and with patients on an immunosuppressive protocol without cyclosporine.

patients who do not receive immunosuppressive therapy have significantly fewer circulating endothelial cells compared with patients who receive cyclosporine and are not significantly different from healthy, untreated controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endothelial cells in the immunological processes that are involved in organ rejection.
the development of a new method for the detection of circulating endothelial cell (CEC) damage in renal transplant recipients.
the study of the endothelium, a thin layer of cells that line the inner surfaces of blood vessels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of calcineurin inhibiting drugs in renal transplantation results in endothelial damage, which is associated with increased numbers of circulating endothelium-derived cells in the peripheral blood.

the use of calcineurin-based immunosuppressive therapy is associated with an increase in circulating CD146+ endothelial cells, which may be an indication of calcineurininhibitor-induced endothelial injury.
calcineurin-inhibitor-induced endothelial cell damage is associated with an increase in the number of circulating endothelial cell in the peripheral blood of renal transplant recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circulating endothelial cells could be a novel marker for the calcineurin induced endothelial damage and could be used for the early prediction of the calcineurine toxicity.
calcineurin inhibition leads to endothelial damage and that this can be detected by the number of circulating endothelial progenitor cells.

the use of immunomagnetic DynaBeads™ for the isolation of circulating endothelial progenitor cells from peripheral blood is an effective method to study the effects of calcineurin-inhibiting immunosuppressants on endothelial progenitor cell function in transplant patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
circulating endothelial cell counts are elevated in patients receiving calcineurin-inhibitor based immunosuppression.
circulating endothelial cell counts are a novel marker for calcineurine-induced endothelial damage.
circulating endothelial progenitor cells are a marker of calcineurin toxicity.
